item.title: US goods trade deficit widens 10.7% to USD 149.5 billion in October as imports surge

item.content:encoded:
US goods trade deficit widens 10.7% to USD 149.5 billion in October as imports surge The United States' goods trade deficit widened by 10.7 per cent month-on-month to USD 149.5 billion in October 2026, compared to USD 135.1 billion in September, as growth in imports outpaced that of exports, according to advance estimates released by the US Census Bureau on Friday. ANI | Updated: 27-11-2026 19:23 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 19:23 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States' goods trade deficit widened by 10.7 per cent month-on-month to USD 149.5 billion in October 2026, compared to USD 135.1 billion in September, as growth in imports outpaced that of exports, according to advance estimates released by the US Census Bureau on Friday. On a year-on-year basis, the goods trade deficit surged by over 143 per cent from USD 61.4 billion recorded in October 2025. "The international trade deficit was $149.5 billion in October, up $14.4 billion from $135.1 billion in September," the US Census Bureau said in its Advance Economic Indicators Report. Goods imports rose by 6.1 per cent month-on-month to USD 365.3 billion in October, while exports increased by 3.2 per cent to USD 215.8 billion. "Exports of goods for October were $215.8 billion, $6.7 billion more than September exports. Imports of goods for October were $365.3 billion, $21.1 billion more than September imports," the report said. On an annual basis, US goods imports surged by 42.4 per cent, significantly outpacing the 10.6 per cent growth in exports. The sharp increase in imports was led by capital goods, which registered an 80 per cent year-on-year growth and an 8.5 per cent sequential increase to USD 171.4 billion in October. Imports of industrial supplies, including petroleum and petroleum products, increased by 33.5 per cent year-on-year, while consumer goods and automotive vehicle imports rose by 16.6 per cent and 8.4 per cent, respectively. On the exports front, capital goods recorded a 29.2 per cent year-on-year increase, while exports of industrial supplies rose by 3.6 per cent. However, exports of automotive vehicles and consumer goods declined by 5 per cent each. The widening of the goods trade deficit comes amid Washington's renewed push for tariffs on its trading partners over alleged structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors. On November 25, the United States Trade Representative (USTR) announced proposed tariff actions following 14 investigations under Section 301 of US trade law. Washington has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, with certain exemptions, while indicating that the rate could be lowered to 17 per cent if India reaches an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade addressing the findings of the investigation. Meanwhile, US wholesale inventories increased by 0.9 per cent month-on-month and 8.5 per cent year-on-year to USD 1,023.4 billion in October. Retail inventories also rose by 0.8 per cent sequentially and 5.1 per cent annually to USD 893.2 billion during the month. The figures are adjusted for seasonal variations but not for price changes. The October trade figures are advance estimates, with complete data to be published in the upcoming US International Trade in Goods and Services report. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Ra’am party chair Mansour Abbas to address "definition of Hamas" on Saturday ahead of Eisenkot coalition push: Report The Times of Israel reported that Abbas is scheduled to make the statement in an interview with journalist Dana Weiss on Channel 12. Confirming the broadcast, Abbas said in a statement carried by Channel 12, “On Saturday night, my interview with [journalist] Dana Weiss will be broadcast on Channel 12 news. I will address the definition of Hamas.”  ANI | The Times Of Israel Reported That Abbas Is Scheduled To Make The Statement In An Interview With Journalist Dana Weiss On Channel 12 Confirming The Broadcast, Abbas Said In A Statement Carried By Channel 12, “On Saturday Night, My Interview With | Updated: 27-11-2026 14:42 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 14:42 IST

Ra’am party chairman Mansour Abbas (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Ra’am party chairman Mansour Abbas is set to publicly declare that he recognises Hamas as a terror group during a television interview on Saturday night, a potential political shift that could clear an obstacle to his Arab-led party joining a coalition headed by Gadi Eisenkot, according to The Times of Israel, citing a Hebrew media report. The Times of Israel reported that Abbas is scheduled to make the statement in an interview with journalist Dana Weiss on Channel 12. Confirming the broadcast, Abbas said in a statement carried by Channel 12, “On Saturday night, my interview with [journalist] Dana Weiss will be broadcast on Channel 12 news. I will address the definition of Hamas.” Abbas added that media coverage should address only “my words in the interview, and not other words attributed to me.” A public designation of Hamas as a terror group would mark a major departure for Abbas, who previously served in Israel’s governing coalition from 2021 to 2022 and ran Jewish candidate Yoav Segalovitz alongside Ra’am ahead of last month’s election to broaden its appeal and signal readiness for a coalition role. Previously, Abbas condemned acts of terror, including Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack, but refrained from labelling Hamas a terror group, arguing that doing so allowed him to serve as a “bridge” and helped protect his family. The Joint List, the other Arab-led party, has likewise not publicly recognised Hamas as a terror group, according to Times of Israel. Eisenkot, who has nine days left on his mandate to form a government, has required every party in his coalition to recognise Hamas as a terror group and pledge its destruction. Meeting that condition could open a path for Ra’am into an Eisenkot-led government and help assemble a majority to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In a teaser for the Saturday evening Channel 12 interview, Weiss asks Abbas to confirm the meaning of a blurred text on a laptop screen before asking, “Have you reconciled yourself to the possibility that this step you’re taking could cost you your life?” Abbas, as quoted by the Times of Israel, replied: “I’ve reconciled myself to it.” According to The Times of Israel, citing a report by Ynet, Ra’am’s entry into an Eisenkot government remains contingent on policy demands, chiefly curbing crime in Arab municipalities, even if the Hamas declaration is made. Earlier, Abbas claimed that his party and the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) would join a proposed government led by Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot, with the Joint List providing parliamentary support from outside the coalition. Speaking in an interview with Radio Makan on Thursday, Abbas said the political bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu was nearing an agreement to establish a new government, The Jerusalem Post reported. Abbas outlined a possible coalition arrangement involving the four parties belonging to the change bloc, alongside UTJ and his United Arab List (Ra’am), with the Joint List extending external parliamentary support. Eisenkot's Yashar party has reportedly indicated that it aims to form a government as early as next week without requesting an extension of its mandate from President Isaac Herzog. While the approval from the Lithuanian ultra-Orthodox leadership could pave the way for formal coalition negotiations, a final decision on joining the prospective government remains pending. (ANI)

item.title: Danny Boyle backs Jack O’Connell as James Bond villain, says actor "would have been a great 007"
item.description: Filmmaker Danny Boyle has backed actor Jack O’Connell as a potential villain in the upcoming James Bond film, while maintaining that the actor would also have been a strong choice to play the iconic ...
item.content:encoded:
Danny Boyle backs Jack O’Connell as James Bond villain, says actor "would have been a great 007" Filmmaker Danny Boyle has backed actor Jack O’Connell as a potential villain in the upcoming James Bond film, while maintaining that the actor would also have been a strong choice to play the iconic British spy, according to Variety.  ANI | Updated: 27-11-2026 09:47 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 09:47 IST

Danny Boyle (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Filmmaker Danny Boyle has backed actor Jack O’Connell as a potential villain in the upcoming James Bond film, while maintaining that the actor would also have been a strong choice to play the iconic British spy, according to Variety. Boyle, who previously starred O’Connell in his film “Ink”, said there had been growing speculation about the actor taking on the antagonist’s role opposite Robert Pattinson, who has been cast as the next James Bond. Speaking on the Alchemy with Anthony Mason podcast, the filmmaker praised both O’Connell and Pattinson for their screen presence, saying they possess an elusive quality that makes audiences want to watch them. “They have that thing where you want to watch them,” Boyle said. “And it’s impossible to quantify what it is, otherwise we’d all buy it for ourselves. But it’s just there, and you want to follow them.” However, Boyle also acknowledged that O’Connell could have been an excellent choice for the lead role, adding that the actor “would have been a great Bond as well," according to Variety. O’Connell was previously believed to have been among the actors considered for the coveted role of 007. Interestingly, Boyle had also expressed support for Pattinson as a potential James Bond years before the actor was reportedly selected for the role. In 2019, after stepping away from directing “No Time to Die” over creative differences, Boyle suggested that Pattinson could replace Daniel Craig as the next 007. At the time, Boyle was particularly impressed by Pattinson's performance in Claire Denis' science-fiction film “High Life”. Speaking in an interview in 2019, he recalled thinking, “It was so bizarre, because I was sitting there thinking: ‘Oh my God, they should get him to be the next Bond.’” Reflecting on Pattinson's casting, Boyle said he had recognised the actor's star potential much earlier, including during his performances in the “Twilight” films. “He’s a movie star, and I could see that from the first ‘Twilight’ films. Him and Kristen Stewart, the two of them. You thought: they’re movie stars. It’s like a given,” he said, according to Variety. “So there’s not that many of them out there. And having a British pedigree will always help him in that world as well,” Boyle added. Boyle was originally attached to direct the 25th James Bond film, “No Time to Die”, but exited the project in 2018 following creative differences with the producers. The film was eventually directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga, with Daniel Craig returning as 007, according to Variety. With Pattinson now set to take on the iconic role, Boyle's latest remarks have also brought renewed attention to O’Connell as a potential addition to the Bond franchise, this time on the other side of the battle. (ANI)
